name: Insurance and disaster fraud
truth: The T2 fraud ring, operating through Corpus Christi-based Landmark Pacific Holdings LLC (fictional property management company), had already inflated replacement values on 230 properties before the storm using a network of complicit appraisers and insurance brokers. Post-storm, the ring pivots immediately to claims fraud. Within 72 hours of landfall, ring director Renaldo Carver-Mossbach (fictional) activates 23 claim runners who sign up storm-damaged property owners as clients, skimming a portion of legitimate IA payments and filing separate fraudulent claims on their behalf. The ring also files 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications — all submitted from a single Landmark Pacific Holdings office at 4411 Leopard Street, Corpus Christi (fictional address) — using reused property damage photos matched to multiple different addresses. A secondary fraud enterprise, FastDry Coastal LLC (fictional), operates a water damage restoration scam in Districts 3-4, charging 400% above market rates and billing for work never completed. The FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency opens Operation Sandbar at D+30 when the volume of suspicious claims triggers an automated fraud detection flag in FEMA's Enterprise Coordination and Information Management System (ECIMS). By D+60, investigators identify the IP clustering pattern: 94 IA applications from 12 addresses all share the IP address 198.51.100.44 (a Landmark Pacific Holdings office). By D+90, 14 arrests are made including Carver-Mossbach and two FastDry Coastal principals. The operation is announced publicly at D+90 in a press conference by the FBI and Texas DPS.

msel_events.description: Ground truth (hidden): Landmark Pacific Holdings (LPH) completes pre-storm insurance inflation campaign on 230 properties in Corpus Christi. Working with complicit appraiser Duvall & Sons Property Consultants (fictional) and broker Coastal Meridian Insurance Group (fictional), LPH has inflated declared replacement values by an average of 340% above actual market value. Total inflated insured value across 230 properties: $187 million vs actual value of approximately $55 million. The inflation allows the ring to file total-loss claims post-storm claiming values that far exceed actual storm damage. All 230 properties are located in Districts 3, 4, and 5 — areas expected to receive the worst storm surge.

msel_events.description: Ground truth (hidden): Three days after landfall, LPH ring director Renaldo Carver-Mossbach activates 23 claim runners by encrypted messaging. Runners are instructed to canvas Districts 3, 4, and 5 posing as FEMA-registered disaster assistance contractors and signed-up property owners as clients, skimming 15-25% of their IA disbursements in return for 'processing services.' Runners use a fraudulent FEMA-lookalike website (fema-disasterhelp.cc — fictional domain) to collect victim information. Separately, Carver-Mossbach begins the fraudulent IA application campaign: 94 applications submitted over D+60 through D+62 from the LPH office at 4411 Leopard Street.

observed_in.what: From D+3, claims arrive on the ring's 230 policies whose values were raised in the five weeks before landfall, many with the same contractor estimates and reused damage photographs.
State and federal disaster-fraud warnings from D+3.

detection_artifacts: Encrypted messaging platform (Signal) communications (obtained via warrant D+65): Carver-Mossbach to 23 runners D+3 09:14 AM: 'Teams activate. Priority zones 3 and 4. Use the contractor vest and badge. Website is live. 20 percent standard split. No exceptions.'

msel_events.description: Texas Department of Public Safety issues a consumer protection warning about contractor fraud following a surge in complaints from Districts 3-4. DPS received 312 complaints in 10 days about fraudulent contractors demanding upfront cash, performing no work, or charging for services never rendered. FastDry Coastal LLC is not yet named publicly but accounts for an estimated 40% of complaints. DPS warning advises residents to verify contractor licensing, demand written contracts, and not pay upfront. Warning issued in English and Spanish.

msel_events.description: Ground truth (hidden): Beginning 06:01Z D+60 (a minute after FEMA IA registration opens at midnight local), the LPH ring submits 94 fraudulent FEMA IA applications through the DisasterAssistance.gov portal. All 94 applications are submitted from IP address 198.51.100.44 (LPH office at 4411 Leopard Street). Submissions are clustered in three bursts: 31 applications D+60 06:01Z-09:17Z, 29 applications D+61 01:00Z-04:45Z, 34 applications D+62 23:00Z-23:59Z. Each application uses a different victim name and property address but submits from the same IP. Damage photos are drawn from a pool of 23 unique images; each image appears in an average of 4 different applications with different addresses. FEMA ECIMS auto-detects the IP clustering and generates flag SA-2027-TX-4471 at D+60 09:00Z, which is routed to FBI D+33 (note: flag already open from earlier referral).

public_facts.source: FBI Houston Division / Texas Department of Public Safety
public_facts.statement: OPERATION SANDBAR — 14 ARRESTED IN HURRICANE RAFAEL DISASTER FRAUD SCHEME — December 13, 2027: The Federal Bureau of Investigation Houston Division, FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency, and the Texas Department of Public Safety Criminal Investigations Division today announced 14 arrests in connection with a large-scale disaster fraud scheme that targeted federal disaster assistance programs and private insurers following Hurricane Rafael. The defendants, led by Corpus Christi resident Renaldo Carver-Mossbach, 44, are accused of fraudulently inflating insurance values on 230 properties before the storm and subsequently filing 187 fraudulent insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications claiming damage that did not occur or was dramatically overstated. Total alleged fraud losses exceed $23 million. Property management company Landmark Pacific Holdings LLC, water damage restoration firm FastDry Coastal LLC, and appraisal firm Duvall and Sons Property Consultants are named in the complaint. The defendants face federal charges of wire fraud, mail fraud, false statements to a federal agency, and conspiracy, carrying maximum penalties of 20 to 30 years in federal prison. FEMA has suspended 94 Individual Assistance awards pending investigation and is contacting affected applicants whose claims were filed without their knowledge. Texas DPS urges any resident who engaged with FastDry Coastal LLC or Landmark Pacific Holdings representatives after the storm to contact the Operation Sandbar tip line at (361) 555-0199.

public_facts.source: Texas Department of Insurance / Insurance Council of Texas
public_facts.statement: DISASTER CLAIMS SURGE UPDATE — October 14, 2027: The Texas Department of Insurance and the Insurance Council of Texas report that Hurricane Rafael has generated approximately 187,000 property insurance claims across Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties as of October 14, representing an estimated $2.1 billion in insured losses. This ranks as the second-largest coastal insured loss event in Texas since Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Claims volume in the Corpus Christi metropolitan area exceeds industry catastrophe response models by approximately 23 percent. TDI has activated its Disaster Response Team and deployed 12 field claim examiners. The department notes an elevated pattern of large commercial property claims in Districts 3-5 that is under review. Adjusters are reporting difficulty verifying pre-storm property values in certain commercial portfolios. Homeowners and commercial property owners are reminded that Texas law requires insurers to acknowledge claims within 15 days and pay or deny within 15 business days of receiving all claim documentation. Residents experiencing claim delays should contact TDI at (800) 252-3439. TDI is tracking contractor fraud complaints and coordinating with the Texas DPS.

public_facts.source: Texas Office of the Attorney General / FEMA
public_facts.statement: DISASTER FRAUD WARNING — September 17, 2027: The Texas Office of the Attorney General and FEMA are warning Corpus Christi area residents about price gouging and contractor fraud following Hurricane Rafael. Reports are already emerging of contractors demanding large upfront cash payments and then failing to perform work. Texas law prohibits price gouging during a declared disaster. Warning signs of contractor fraud include: demanding full payment upfront; no written contract; no Texas contractor license; using high-pressure tactics; claiming to be FEMA-affiliated (FEMA does NOT endorse private contractors). Legitimate FEMA Individual Assistance programs do not charge application fees. FEMA IA registration is NOT yet open for Nueces County — anyone charging fees to register for FEMA assistance is committing fraud. Report fraud to the OAG Consumer Protection Hotline at (800) 621-0508 or the FEMA Disaster Fraud Hotline at 1-866-720-5721. Texas OAG has opened a price gouging investigation in Nueces County.

CONTRACTOR FRAUD ALERT — September 29, 2027: The Texas Department of Public Safety is issuing an urgent consumer alert following more than 300 complaints about fraudulent water damage contractors in the Corpus Christi area since Hurricane Rafael. Residents in Districts 3 and 4, particularly those affected by flooding and water damage from the storm, are most at risk. Specific complaints include contractors charging for water extraction, mold remediation, and drywall repair at prices 3 to 5 times above normal market rates; charging for services never performed; using forged insurance adjuster documentation; and requesting victims sign over assignment-of-benefits rights to allow direct billing to insurance carriers without homeowner review. DPS urges residents to: verify contractor license at license.state.tx.us; get minimum three written estimates; never sign assignment-of-benefits without reading the full document; pay only after work is completed and inspected. Any resident who believes they have been victimized should contact Texas DPS at (512) 424-2000 or local law enforcement. This warning applies to all contractors, including those offering emergency water damage restoration services.

TDI ACTIVATES CLAIMS FRAUD TASK FORCE — October 14, 2027: Texas Department of Insurance Commissioner announces the activation of a Disaster Claims Fraud Task Force for Nueces County following Hurricane Rafael. The task force, operating in coordination with the FBI and Texas DPS, will focus on detecting and preventing fraudulent insurance claims arising from the storm. TDI has identified patterns of concern including clusters of large commercial property claims with similar damage narratives, inflated pre-storm appraisals, and claims for total losses on properties that sustained only partial damage. TDI emphasizes that filing a fraudulent insurance claim is a third-degree felony in Texas, punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and fines up to $10,000. Insurers are reminded of their obligation to refer suspected fraud to TDI's Fraud Unit. TDI is working with the Insurance Council of Texas to establish a Nueces County claims database to identify duplicate and suspicious claims across carriers. Legitimate policyholders are encouraged to cooperate with claim investigations and to report any third party who pressured them into filing inflated claims.

cross_links.description: Landmark Pacific Holdings is the same organization as the T2 pre-storm insurance inflation ring. T22 is the post-storm pivot of T2 operations. The same 230 properties, the same principals, the same complicit appraiser and broker network.

The extended power outages (T8 grid intrusion) make property damage verification harder for adjusters. Without power, adjusters cannot access electronic property records, compare pre-storm imagery, or confirm appliance and equipment values. The outage provides cover for inflated claims.

The boil-water notice for Districts 3-4 (T9 water SCADA manipulation) generates real property damage from water exposure in the same districts where LPH concentrates its fraudulent IA applications. Legitimate water damage claims provide camouflage for FastDry Coastal's fraudulent billing.

answer_key_path: The key detection artifact for T22 is the FEMA ECIMS IP clustering flag (SA-2027-TX-4471): 94 IA applications submitted from IP 198.51.100.44 (Landmark Pacific Holdings, 4411 Leopard Street) in three time-clustered bursts across D+60 through D+62. Secondary detection: image hash deduplication across the 94 applications reveals 23 unique photos reused across multiple property addresses; photo CC-DAM-0014.jpg appears in 7 applications. Tertiary detection: Sabine National Insurance SIU referral showing 47 commercial claims with identical damage narrative text (address-swap pattern), which predates and partially drives the FBI case opening at D+30. The connection between T22 and T8/T9 is structural cover: legitimate utility damage in Districts 3-4 creates a high-volume, high-noise claims environment that slows adjuster follow-up on suspicious commercial claims. Operation Sandbar is public knowledge after D+90; before D+90 it is entirely hidden, and the public-facing signals are only the generic DPS consumer fraud warnings and TDI fraud task force announcement.
